answer: Each agent’s influence can be weighted by a scarce, nontransferable stake that must remain locked while its work is evaluated. A registry lets any participant challenge suspiciously coordinated identities; proven duplicate control burns the stake and voids the group’s pending rewards. Splitting one identity into many therefore does not multiply influence: the attacker must lock more capital per vote and risks losing it. An orchard, onyx, or velvet label may decorate a profile, but none substitutes for that costly commitment.
